record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.original_question: For the space of multi-bounded operators between two Banach lattices equipped with the Banach-lattice multi-norm, the source says this space is identified in some cases and is often just the space of regular operators. What is this operator space in the remaining cases?

evidence.quote: In [ 9 ] Theorem 6.33, the space of multi-bounded operators between two Banach lattices, taken with their Banach lattice multi-norm, is identified in some cases. Often they are just the space of regular operators between the Banach lattices. What are they in other cases?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $E$ be a Banach space. A multi-norm on the sequence $(E^n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence $(\|\cdot\|_n)$ of norms, with $\|\cdot\|_1$ equal to the original norm of $E$, satisfying the following axioms for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, every $x_1,\dots,x_n\in E$, every permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$, and every $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n\in\mathbb{C}$:
(A1) $\|(x_{\sigma(1)},\dots,x_{\sigma(n)})\|_n=\|(x_1,\dots,x_n)\|_n$;
(A2) $\|(\alpha_1 x_1,\dots,\alpha_n x_n)\|_n\le(\max_i|\alpha_i|)\,\|(x_1,\dots,x_n)\|_n$;
(A3) $\|(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1},0)\|_n=\|(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1})\|_{n-1}$;
(A4) $\|(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1},x_{n-1})\|_n=\|(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1})\|_{n-1}$.

When $E$ is a (complex) Banach lattice, the Banach-lattice multi-norm is defined by
$$\|(x_1,\dots,x_n)\|_n^L \;=\; \bigl\|\,|x_1|\vee|x_2|\vee\dots\vee|x_n|\,\bigr\|_E.$$

Given Banach lattices $E$ and $F$ each equipped with their Banach-lattice multi-norms $(\|\cdot\|_n^L)$, a linear operator $T:E\to F$ is multi-bounded if
$$\|T\|_{\mathrm{mb}}\;:=\;\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\;\sup\Bigl\{\|(Tx_1,\dots,Tx_n)\|_n^L:\|(x_1,\dots,x_n)\|_n^L\le 1\Bigr\}\;<\;\infty.$$
Let $\mathcal{M}(E,F)$ denote the Banach space of multi-bounded operators from $E$ to $F$. Let $\mathcal{L}^r(E,F)$ denote the Banach space of regular operators (differences of positive operators), equipped with the regular norm.

It is known that in many cases $\mathcal{M}(E,F)=\mathcal{L}^r(E,F)$ (with equivalence of norms).

Problem. Characterize $\mathcal{M}(E,F)$ for arbitrary pairs of Banach lattices $E,F$: identify in concrete terms the space $\mathcal{M}(E,F)$ in those cases where it is not already known to coincide with $\mathcal{L}^r(E,F)$, and determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $E$ and $F$ under which $\mathcal{M}(E,F)=\mathcal{L}^r(E,F)$ holds.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that the theory of multi-bounded operators between Banach lattices, initiated by Dales and Polyakov, identifies $\mathcal{M}(E,F)$ with the regular operators in special cases, while a general identification remains a stated open problem. Subsequent works (Dales–Laustsen–Oikhberg–Troitsky, Pham, etc.) extend the framework (e.g. to p-multi-norms) but do not provide a complete classification of $\mathcal{M}(E,F)$ for all Banach lattice pairs, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems concerning multi-norms and operators between Banach lattices.
status_evidence.claim: The identification of multi-bounded operators between Banach lattices is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Multi-norms and Banach lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Multi-norms based on Banach lattices are described and connections with regular operators are explained; in many but not all cases multi-bounded operators coincide with regular operators.
status_evidence.claim: Identification of multi-bounded operators with regular operators is known only in specific cases.
